html:
SMTO-SKL-0120 — This Slack sign-in belongs to a different account or workspace

GUID: 60ecf312-22d0-5e18-938a-202a43e81e19
Slug: slack-identity-mismatch
Domain: SKL · Subsystem: slack

What happened

  • SMTO didn't accept the Slack approval because the Slack workspace or account you approved doesn't match the one this saved connection is for. SMTO did not save it over your existing connection.

How to fix — simple steps

  1. In your browser, check which Slack workspace and account you're signed in to. Switch to the ones this connection was first made with. SMTO only accepts an approval from the same workspace and account the saved connection belongs to.
  2. Ask the Agent to connect Slack again with the same Slack OAuth App and the same workspace key (the name this Slack connection is saved under). Approve the request on the Slack page that opens. Reconnecting under the same name with the matching account restores the connection instead of creating a second one.
  3. If you really want a different Slack account, workspace, or a bot instead of your own account, ask the Agent to connect it under a new workspace key. Each saved Slack connection stands for exactly one workspace and one account, so a different one needs its own name.

What success looks like

  • The Agent reports Slack as connected, and asking it to list your Slack workspaces shows the workspace and account you expected.

If it still fails

  • Select Copy error details and send them, with the workspace and account you approved, to the person who manages your Slack app for SMTO. Don't edit the saved Slack Workspace entry in Parameter Store by hand to make it match; use a new workspace key instead.

Technical details

Observed condition

  • The Slack OAuth exchange or token refresh returned an identity (team, user or bot ID, enterprise ID, or token_type) that disagrees with auth.test or with the saved slack_workspace profile, so the grant was rejected.

What this means

  • Slack identity verification fails, returned token type differs, or saved team/user/bot/app identity conflicts with the new authorization. The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.

Why this can happen

  • Slack identity verification fails, returned token type differs, or saved team/user/bot/app identity conflicts with the new authorization.

How to diagnose it

  • Distinguish failed verification from a concrete identity mismatch using safe fields.

How to fix it

  • Compare the approving team and user with the saved slack_workspace profile's workspace_id, user_id, principal_type and oauth_app_ref in Parameter Store. Rerun slack.connect with the same auth_app_ref and workspace_key while signed into the original team and principal, or use a new workspace_key for a different identity; a Slack OAuth App whose flow (user vs workspace) differs from the saved principal_type also triggers this.
  • Authorize the expected Slack team and user or bot. Use a new profile key for a different identity.

Retry and execution caution

  • Inspect exact provider state and authority first.

How to verify the fix

  • Verified team and principal match the intended profile, or a deliberate new profile is created for another identity.

What not to do

  • Do not expose secrets or blindly replay uncertain mutations.

Technical notes

  • The diagnostic performs no Slack request. Inspect the original receipt and operation stage to determine effects; keep workspace, principal and exact channel/message identities fixed during recovery.
  • Preserve the occurrence ID and safe request/operation references. Receipts and occurrence facts establish what started or completed; the catalog does not authorize retries or establish execution outcome.
